discovery: Theoretical prediction and experimental discovery of topological insulators and the quantum spin Hall effect
rationale: Topological insulators are among the most cited and longest-standing Nobel-calibre advances in condensed matter that have not yet been recognised. They build on the 2016 prize for topological phases. Kane and Mele predicted the quantum spin Hall state and the Z2 invariant, and Molenkamp's group first observed it in HgTe quantum wells. Shoucheng Zhang co-originated the HgTe prediction but died in 2018, which makes this trio the natural one. The committee has awarded quantum and condensed-matter work before, and this field now has broad acclaim, major awards (Breakthrough, Dirac, Buckley) and lasting impact.
